title: Crack spread reversion: the 3:2:1 refining margin, October 2006 to April 2024
question: On rolled NYMEX WTI crude oil, RBOB gasoline and heating oil futures from 2006-10-02 to 2024-04-05, does trading the 3:2:1 crack spread back towards its one-year mean (enter beyond 2 standard deviations, exit at the mean, weekly) have a positive Sharpe ratio that passes at least four of the five reality tests, after 3 bp per unit traded and 2 bp per roll?
prior_trials_note: 315 (REG-0009's floor) + 1 (REG-0009's energy_book), counted across all families as the project has so far. No version of this rule has been evaluated. This is a floor: it does not include the always-on search's variations (engine/output/search.db on the owner's machine), which have never included energy futures because fut.* is not on main yet.
what_would_change_our_mind: A pass would give the project an energy strategy that does not depend on the oil price, worth a forward test once futures prices after April 2024 are available (RES-0019). A fail would say the spread's ties to refining are too slow or too seasonal for a one-year z-score rule, and a seasonal version would need its own registration counted as a further trial.
already_seen: No. Before registering, only unit tests on made-up prices were run (spread arithmetic, trade direction, entry and exit thresholds, leg sizes, no look-ahead, and a mutation check). No return, Sharpe ratio or other performance number was computed for crack_spread_reversion, and the crack spread itself was not computed or plotted on real prices.
